cells.tense: The practice now carries its own weight, and the clearing, when it comes, is welcome.
cells.act: let one structure collapse that could not hold
cells.ask: A routine at the bench has gone hollow — some rule about doing it right that no longer earns its keep. Stop propping it up. Watch what comes down, and change nothing else about the work.
cells.core:
The work is going well in a particular way: the small daily session gets done because you like it, not because a whip hangs nearby. Time alone at the bench leaves you more connected to people, not less. And when something built on a bad premise gives way, you feel the relief — less to carry, not a loss.
The refinement hasn't turned on you. So you can afford to be careless with the routine that's gone hollow. Stop holding it up and watch. What was true in it stays; what falls was only keeping its shape. Clearing is not the reward waiting at the end of practice. It is part of the practice.
cells.sheetLine: The practice holds. Let one hollow thing fall.
cells.verb: keeping a small light lit by turning up
cells.place: at the bench where the strict thing is kept

cells.tense: Keeping the light lit will have become the thing you cannot put down, and you brace for what happens if you do.
cells.act: let go of the thing you are gripping
cells.ask: Release, for a day, the outcome your hands are tightest around — the result, the unbroken run. The practice stays. Only the grip goes. See what has held by evening.
cells.core:
The practice is still daily, but it no longer feels chosen — it feels like a wall that would come down if you stopped holding it, so you can't stop. The refining has picked up speed: nothing finishes, everything could be better, and the hours alone have stopped connecting you to anyone. You're not practicing toward something now; you're practicing to keep the ceiling up.
Trying harder doesn't fix this. Set down the result you hold hardest — not the whole practice, the grip on that one outcome — and leave your hands empty for a while. If the day is uncomfortable, that's information: something there is being held by force. Whatever remains after you loosen is yours.

cells.tense: The bench has sat unused for a long while, and the daily session happens somewhere else now.
cells.act: trade one thing for one thing, and keep no score
cells.ask: Offer one person one small concrete thing — an hour, a hand with a task — and ask one real thing back that you need. Keep it even, then let the matter close.
cells.core:
The quiet work of getting better at something is real and it is yours, but it sits in the same place as something that landed wrong, and you have stayed away. What's there is skill you don't use and tools going dusty. The clearing this place is named for doesn't get to happen, because nothing new gets built there to clear.
Don't force the sitting-down. Start where giving and getting still move. Offer one person one real thing, ask one real thing back, and stop the ledger there — no overpaying to stay safe, no score kept afterward. Trade small and even. A practice held in fair exchange with someone else is easier to pick up than one held alone.
cells.sheetLine: The bench has been empty a long time. Start with a fair trade.

cells.tense: The work is being done and nobody is claiming to do it, least of all the one at the bench.
cells.act: sketch the whole of it badly, on one page, and keep the sketch
cells.ask: Take what you're already good at and put its rough whole onto a single page — the start, the daily doing, where it goes. No polish. Leave the page where you'll see it.
cells.core:
The skill is real and it got that way on purpose, one small session at a time, over years, whether or not anyone kept count. Ask how it happened and the answer comes back as 'it just does' — some of that is modesty, and some is that the sessions have stopped reading as yours. What you can do now was made by a practice whose author has stepped out.
Put it down on paper, roughly. Draw the whole shape of what you're good at — where it started, what you do most days, where it's headed — one page, no art to it. Not a plan, just a rendering in your own hand, kept where you'll run into it. The work itself carries on exactly as it has.
cells.sheetLine: You've been at the bench the whole time. Put it on paper.
